MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  SPECIAL MEETING
  MARCH 4, 2025
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  5:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Stewart called the meeting to order at 3 :01 pm.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Doug Stewart; Mayor Pro Tem Marianne Riggins;’ and
  Councilmembers Haylynn Conrad, Bruce Silverstein and Steve Uhring.

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Joseph Toney, Assistant City
  Manager; Alexis Brown, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey Pettijohn, City Clerk; Yolanda
  Bundy, Environmental Sustainability Director; Maureen Tamuri, Interim Flaming
  Director; Parker Davis, Media Technician; Christina Munoz, Deputy City Clerk; Barbara
  Esparza; Human Resources Technician; Matt Myerhoff, Media Information Officer; Larbi
  Azzaz; Assistant Planner; Courtney Brown, Associate Planner; Alexander da Silva,
  Assistant Planner; Gail Duncan, Administrative Assistant; Tyler Eaton, Principal Planner;
  Samantha Elias, Associate Planner; Rebecca Evans; Senior Management Analyst; and
  Aakash Shah, Contract Planner

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Drew Leonard led the Pledge of Allegiance.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettij ohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on March
  3, 2025.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Uhring seconded a motion
  to approve the agenda. The motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 1  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment on the Consent Calendar.

  Howard Rudzki declined the opportunity to speak.

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Stewart returned the matter to the
  table for discussion.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of March 4, 2025
  Page 2 of 4

,  MOTION  Councilmember Uhring moved, and Mayor Pro Tern Riggins seconded a motion to
  approve the Consent Calendar. The motion carried unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previouslv Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Waive Further Reading
  Recommended Action: After the City Attorney has read the title, waive full
  reading of ordinances considered on this agenda for introduction on first
  reading and/or second reading and adoption.
  2.  Confirmation of the Director of Emergency Services Order Relating to the
  Palisades Fire Recovery
  Recommended Action: Confirm the Order of the Director of Emergency
  Services dated February 28, 2025, directing law enforcement to set up and
  police resident-only access checkpoints at specified roads in response to the
  Palisades Fire recovery and extending the order through March l4, 2025.

  ITEM 2  DISASTER REBUILD ORDINANCE WORKSHOP

  A.  Disaster Rebuild Ordinance Workshop
  The City Council will hold a workshop on the proposed Local Coastal Program
  Amendment and Zoning Text Amendment for rebuilding structures damaged or
  destroyed by natural disasters, including but not limited to, the 2025 Palisades Fire,
  2024 Franklin Fire, and 2024 Broad Fire. Members of the public will have the
  opportunity to speak with Councilmembers and subject matter experts in an open
  dialogue and will not be limited to normal public comment time limits.

  Deputy City Manager Brown introduced the workshop and explained the process.

  Mayor Stewart and Councilmember Uhring announced the deadline for the right of
  entry forms for tire debris removal.

  Colonel Sawser, US Army Corps of Engineers, discussed the importance of filing
  right of entry forms.

  Principal Planner Eaton presented an overview of the proposed Local Coastal
  Program and Malibu Municipal Code amendments.

  The Councilmembers left the dais and joined three discussion groups on the floor
  of the Chambers. Councilmember Silverstein and Councilmember Uhring
  participated in discussion group one, Councilmember Conrad and Mayor Pro Tem
  Riggins participated in discussion group two, and Mayor Stewart participated in the
  virtual discussion group.

  The discussion groups discussed and asked questions regarding the following
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of March 4, 2025
  Page 3 of 4

  topics: Primary Development Area, Temporary Housing Provisions, Coastal
  Development Permit Exemptions and De Minimis Waivers, Accessory Dwelling
  Units, Primary View Determinations and View Impacts, Rebuild Standards for
  Non-Conforming Structures, and Permitting Process. Each group reported out the
  issues discussed by their group for each topic.

  RECESS  At 6:18 p.m., Mayor Stewart recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at 6:20
  pm. with all Councilmembers present and the discussion groups continued their
  review of the proposed ordinance.

  At 8:35 p.m., the Councilmember returned to the dais.

  The Council discussed the feedback from the workshop and provided direction to
  staff.

  ITEM 3  ORDINANCES AND PUBLIC HEARINGS

  A.  Local Coastal Program Amendment No. 25-001 and Zoning Text Amendment No.
  25—001 — An amendment to the Malibu Local Coastal Program and Malibu
  Municipal Code Title 17 (Zoning) Modifying Standards and Procedures to
  Facilitate the Rebuilding of Structures Damaged or Destroyed bv the 2025
  Palisades Fire, 2024 Franklin Fire, and 2024 Broad Fire
  Recommended Action: l) After the City Attorney reads the title of the ordinance,
  adopt Urgency Ordinance No. 524U, approving Zoning Text Amendment No. 25—
  001, an amendment to Title 17 (Zoning) of the Malibu Municipal Code updating
  regulations to facilitate the rebuilding of structures damaged or destroyed by natural
  disasters, including but not limited to, the 2025 Palisades Fire, 2024 Franklin Fire,
  and 2024 Broad Fire to provide relief for those affected, declaring the urgency
  thereof, and finding the amendments are exempt from the California Environmental
  Quality Act; 2) After the City Attorney reads the title of the ordinance, introduce
  on first reading Ordinance No. 524 approving Local Coastal Program Amendment
  No. 25-001, an amendment to the Local Coastal Program and Zoning Text
  Amendment No. 25-001, an amendment to Title 17 (Zoning) of the Malibu
  Municipal Code updating regulations to facilitate the rebuilding of structures
  damaged or destroyed by natural disasters, including but not limited to, the 2025
  Palisades Fire, 2024 Franklin Fire, and 2024 Broad Fire to provide relief for those
  affected, and finding the amendments are exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act; and 3) Direct staff to schedule second reading and
  adoption of Ordinance No. 524.

  This item was continued to the March 4, 2025 Adjourned Special Meeting.

  ADJOURNMENT

L5  At 8:47 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem Riggins moved, and Councilmember Silverstein seconded a
  motion to adjourn the meeting to March 4, 2025 at 3:00 p.m. The motion carried
  unanimously.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of March 4, 2025
  Page 4 of 4

  Approved and adopted by the City Council of the
  Ci ofMalibu on June 9, 2025.

  MARIANNE RIGGI'NSMayor
